content: 1. Gatifloxacin is the fluoroquinolone most likely to cause dysglycemia, while moxifloxacin is the least likely. Dysglycemia can manifest as either hyperglycemia or hypoglycemia. Close monitoring of blood glucose levels is recommended when using these agents, especially in patients with diabetes or those on insulin therapy. 2. Moxifloxacin can enhance the effects of regular human insulin through pharmacodynamic synergy. This necessitates careful monitoring of blood glucose levels to avoid hypoglycemia. 3. The administration of quinolone antibiotics, including moxifloxacin, may lead to alterations in blood glucose levels, either hyperglycemia or hypoglycemia. Gatifloxacin is particularly associated with this risk, while moxifloxacin has a lower likelihood. 4. Iron dextran complex reduces the absorption of moxifloxacin in the gastrointestinal tract, leading to decreased drug levels. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Alternative therapies should be considered. 5. Iron sucrose also decreases moxifloxacin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction is specific to oral formulations. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 6. Isoflurane and moxifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of arrhythmias. Alternative therapies are recommended to avoid this serious interaction. 7. Moxifloxacin and isotretinoin may increase the risk of phototoxicity due to pharmacodynamic synergy. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but caution is advised. 8. Itraconazole and moxifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Although the clinical significance is unclear, close monitoring is recommended. 9. Ivosidenib and moxifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of torsades de pointes. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. If unavoidable, monitor the QTc interval closely. 10. Ketoconazole and moxifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or consider alternative therapies. 11. Moxifloxacin and ketoprofen may increase the risk of central nervous system (CNS) stimulation and seizures, particularly at high doses of fluoroquinolones. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. 12. Moxifloxacin and ketorolac (including intranasal formulations) may increase the risk of CNS stimulation and seizures. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 13. Lanthanum carbonate reduces moxifloxacin levels by binding cations in the gastrointestinal tract. Administer oral quinolones at least 1 hour before or 4 hours after lanthanum to minimize this interaction. 14. Lapatinib and moxifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. 15. Lefamulin and moxifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. 16. Lenvatinib and moxifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. ECG monitoring is recommended when these drugs are co-administered. 17. Leuprolide increases the toxicity of moxifloxacin by prolonging the QTc interval, raising the risk of torsades de pointes. Close monitoring is required. 18. Levofloxacin and moxifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. 19. Levoketoconazole and moxifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. 20. Moxifloxacin may reduce the efficacy of oral contraceptives containing levonorgestrel, ethinyl estradiol, and ferrous bisglycinate by altering intestinal flora. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution is advised. 21. Lithium and moxifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. 22. Lofepramine and moxifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. 23. Lofexidine and moxifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. ECG monitoring is recommended. 24. Moxifloxacin increases the levels of loprazolam, lorazepam, and lormetazepam by reducing their metabolism. The clinical significance of these interactions is unknown. 25. Lumefantrine and moxifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. 26. Macimorelin and moxifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. Allow sufficient washout time for QT-prolonging drugs before administering macimorelin. 27. Magnesium salts (chloride, citrate, hydroxide, oxide, sulfate) reduce moxifloxacin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Administer magnesium 4 hours before or 8 hours after moxifloxacin to minimize this interaction. 28. Maprotiline and moxifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. 29. Mavorixafor and moxifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Monitor QTc during treatment, especially in patients with risk factors for QTc prolongation. Dose reduction or discontinuation of mavorixafor may be required. 30. Mefenamic acid, meloxicam, and moxifloxacin may increase the risk of CNS stimulation and seizures. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 31. Moxifloxacin may reduce the efficacy of mestranol-containing oral contraceptives by altering intestinal flora. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution is advised. 32. Moxifloxacin enhances the effects of metformin and miglitol through pharmacodynamic synergy. Monitor blood glucose levels closely to avoid hypoglycemia. 33. Methadone and moxifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. 34. Methyl aminolevulinate and moxifloxacin may increase each other's phototoxic effects. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. 35. Methylprednisolone and moxifloxacin may increase the risk of tendon rupture when co-administered. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Moxifloxacin reduces the efficacy of oral microbiota by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Complete antibiotic regimens 2–4 days before initiating oral microbiota therapy. 37. Midazolam levels may increase with moxifloxacin due to reduced metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 38. Mifepristone and moxifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Use alternatives if available and monitor closely. 39. Mirtazapine and moxifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. 40. Mometasone inhaled and moxifloxacin may increase the risk of tendon rupture. Use caution and monitor closely. 41. Nabumetone, naproxen, and moxifloxacin may increase the risk of CNS stimulation and seizures. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 42. Nateglinide and moxifloxacin may enhance each other's effects, increasing the risk of hypoglycemia. Monitor blood glucose levels closely. 43. Nilotinib and moxifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. 44. Nortriptyline and moxifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. 45. Octreotide and moxifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. 46. Olanzapine and moxifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. 47. Olodaterol inhaled and moxifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of ventricular arrhythmias. Use caution and monitor closely. 48. Ondansetron and moxifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration in patients with congenital long QT syndrome. ECG monitoring is recommended in high-risk patients. 49. Osilodrostat and osimertinib both prolong the QTc interval when combined with moxifloxacin. Conduct periodic ECG and electrolyte monitoring. 50. Oxaliplatin and moxifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. 51. Oxaprozin and moxifloxacin may increase the risk of CNS stimulation and seizures. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 52. Oxazepam levels may increase with moxifloxacin due to reduced metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 53. Ozanimod and moxifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid initiating ozanimod in patients concurrently treated with QT-prolonging drugs. 54. Paliperidone and moxifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. 55. Panobinostat and moxifloxacin both significantly prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. 56. Pantothenic acid levels may decrease with moxifloxacin due to altered intestinal flora. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 57. Paroxetine and moxifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. 58. Pasireotide and moxifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. 59. Pazopanib and moxifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 60. Pentamidine and moxifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration is contraindicated. 61. Perphenazine and moxifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. 62. Phenytoin levels may be affected by moxifloxacin through an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 63. Pimozide and moxifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration is contraindicated. 64. Pioglitazone and moxifloxacin may enhance each other's effects, increasing the risk of hypoglycemia. Monitor blood glucose levels closely. 65. Piroxicam and moxifloxacin may increase the risk of CNS stimulation and seizures. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 66. Pitolisant and moxifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. 67. Polysaccharide iron reduces moxifloxacin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. 68. Posaconazole and moxifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. 69. Prednisolone and moxifloxacin may increase the risk of tendon rupture. Use caution and monitor closely.
